# Side-by-side diff

Two versions of one text in two panes, each change opposite its replacement, falling back to one column when narrow.

Status: Experimental. Its API may change in a minor release, without a deprecation first.

Two versions of one text side by side: the old in one pane, the new in the other, each change opposite its replacement. Pass `before` and `after` and the diff is worked out for you (`diffLines`), or pass a unified `diff` or `hunks` as to `FileDiff`.

- **Lines never wrap; the panes scroll.** In code and config the indentation is the structure, and two wrapped panes stop lining up row for row. Each pane scrolls sideways with the scroll-edge cue, the two scroll together, and both are as wide as the longest line on either side, so the column being compared stays opposite itself.
- **Below 48rem it is one column.** The panes are a container query: a phone, or a side panel on a wide screen, gets the unified lines `FileDiff` draws, wrapped, because there is no room for two panes of code.
- **Two regions, read in turn.** Each pane is a focusable region named by its label and the title. A screen reader hears the old version, then the new, each changed line prefixed “Removed:” or “Added:”; the blank rows that keep the panes aligned are hidden from it.
- **State is never colour alone.** A changed line is a wash, a +/− glyph and a word. The gutter stays put while the code scrolls under it, and is hidden from assistive technology and from a copy.
- **Composed, not copied.** The same parser, pairing, glyphs and `ChangeCount` as `FileDiff`, and it sits in a `ChangeReview` beside FileDiffs.

## Usage

### When to use

- Comparing a prompt, a policy or a config with an agent’s revision of it, line against line.
- You hold both versions rather than a patch: pass before and after and the diff is worked out.
- A reviewer has to read across, comparing a changed line with the one it replaces.

### When not to

- One file among several in a proposed change, with hunks to fold. Use [FileDiff](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/ai-change-review--overview.md).
- A change to a record’s fields rather than to lines of text. Use [FieldChanges](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/ai-change-review--overview.md).
- A single version of code or a payload, with nothing to compare it to. Use [CodeBlock](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/components-data-display-code--overview.md).

### Do and don’t

- Do: Name the panes for what the versions are, such as Live and Proposed.
- Don’t: Leave both panes as Before and After when the reader needs to know which one is running.
- Do: Put it inside a ChangeReview when an agent proposes the change, so the comparison and the decision sit together.
- Don’t: Show a proposed change in a diff with no way to approve or reject it.

### Content

- Title it by what is compared, “System prompt, support triage agent”, not by the action.
- Keep pane labels to one or two words; they name the scroll regions.

## Anatomy

The root carries `data-slot="side-by-side-diff"`; each part carries its `data-part`.

1. Container (`[data-slot="side-by-side-diff"]`): A keylined section named by its title, and the container the two-pane query measures.
2. Title (`[data-part="title"]`): What is being compared, as a heading.
3. Count (`[data-part="count"]`): Lines added and removed: “+2 −1” to the eye, a sentence to a screen reader.
4. Pane (`[data-part="pane"]`): One version. Its code scrolls sideways under the scroll-edge cue, in step with the other pane.
5. Pane label (`[data-part="pane-label"]`): Which version this is; it names the pane’s scroll region.
6. Hunk header (`[data-part="hunk-header"]`): The range and section, held at the start while the pane scrolls.
7. Line (`[data-part="line"]`): One line of the version. A change is a wash, a glyph and a hidden word.
8. Gutter (`[data-part="gutter"]`): Line number and +/− glyph, held in place while the code scrolls, never copied.
9. Blank row (`[data-part="filler"]`): Keeps the panes aligned where one side has no line, in the empty texture, hidden from screen readers.

## API

### `SideBySideDiff` (component)

Two versions of one text, side by side: the old in one pane, the new in the other, each change opposite its replacement.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | What is being compared, as a heading: “System prompt, triage agent”. |
| `after` | `string` |  | The text after the change. |
| `afterLabel` | `string` | `After` | The new pane's name. Defaults to “After”. |
| `before` | `string` |  | The text before the change. With `after`, the diff is worked out for you. |
| `beforeLabel` | `string` | `Before` | The old pane's name, shown above it and naming its scroll region. Defaults to “Before”. |
| `context` | `number` | `3` | Unchanged lines kept around each change when the diff is worked out from `before` and `after`. Defaults to 3. |
| `diff` | `string` |  | Or one unified diff, as `git diff` prints it. Wins over `before` and `after`. |
| `headingLevel` | `3 \| 4 \| 5` | `4` | Heading level for the title. Defaults to 4, under a `ChangeReview` heading. |
| `hunks` | `readonly (DiffHunk \| DiffHunkInput)[]` |  | Or the hunks, structured. Wins over `diff`. |

`className`, `ref`, `id` and the other DOM props go to `<section data-slot="side-by-side-diff">`.

Types: `SideBySideDiffProps`

## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus to the old pane, then the new one; a focused pane scrolls sideways with the arrow keys. |

### Mola handles

- The diff is a section named by its title, and each pane a focusable region named by its label and the title, so a keyboard can scroll it and a screen reader can jump to it.
- Changed lines say “Removed:” or “Added:”, and carry a +/− glyph as well as the wash; line numbers and glyphs are hidden from screen readers and from a copy.
- The blank rows that keep the panes aligned are hidden from screen readers, so each pane reads as its version, in order.
- The panes scroll together and carry the scroll-edge cue while there is more to the side; below 48rem they become one column of wrapped lines.
- Code is pinned left to right, so a right-to-left page does not reorder a line of source.

### You handle

- Give it a `title` that says what is compared, and pane labels that say which version is which.
- Set `headingLevel` so the title fits the page outline.
